Title: Local Reviews (2026) | Product Hunt
## Local. ## Zero (!) friction local AI for your Mac. ## Zero (!) friction local AI for your Mac. Local is a macOS app that runs fully private AI directly on your own machine. We built it for completely frictionless setup. It tunes itself to your hardware, so chat, coding agents and meeting notes run up to 5.4x faster on the same hardware, without your data ever leaving the device. "Office Mode" let's you run AI on the fastest machine in the office and every laptop can connect to it. # Local Reviews. ### The community submitted 1 review to tell us what they like about Local, what Local can do better, and more. No reviews yetBe the first to leave a founder review for Local. #### What's great. I've been meaning to run a local model on my Mac for a while but always bounced off the setup - picking the right quantization, figuring out what my hardware could actually handle, getting a decent frontend on top of it. Local just skips all of that. It looked at my machine, picked models that actually run well, and I had a working local chat in a few minutes with zero config decisions to make. The speed difference versus the same models run through a generic wrapper is very noticeable too, meeting notes transcribe close to real time on my M-series Mac. #### What needs improvement. the "Office Mode" feature needs clearer docs on the security side - it's not obvious from the app whether the shared machine's AI service is authenticated or just open to anyone on the same network. I'd also like to see a way to pin a specific model instead of letting it re-optimize picks after a hardware or macOS update. #### vs Alternatives. I'd used LM Studio before and it's solid, but it still puts the model-picking decision on you - you're choosing quantization levels and reading VRAM requirements yourself. Local removes that decision entirely instead of just making the UI around it nicer, which was the actual barrier for me.

results.title: Review: Code review on your own machine, with your own AI | Product Hunt
results.content:
Hi Product Hunt! I'm Hamed, and I made Review.  
  
I'm a developer and team lead. Since AI started writing so much of our code, reviewing it all has become the hardest part of my job. So I built Review: a desktop app for reviewing pull requests, where you can set up a team of AI reviewers from different providers to take the first pass. You still decide what gets published.  
  
What it does:  
- Opens your local Git branches and GitHub pull requests in one window. ⌘P jumps to any of them.  
- Pins each review to exact commits, so the diff doesn't shift when someone pushes.  
- Keeps your comments on your machine until you publish them to GitHub as a review. [...] Subscribe

Launch Team / Built With [...] - Adds an AI reviewer if you want one: OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, or a local model in Ollama or LM Studio. Your keys are stored in the system keychain.  
  
What's different about the AI part: it checks every change against a fixed set of rules (bugs, security, error handling, tests and more), and it shows which rules it actually checked, not just what it found. If a request fails, you can retry only the rules it missed. It can also call your MCP servers for context the code doesn't have, like the ticket behind a change.  
  
It's free, open source (MIT) and needs no account. It runs on macOS, Windows and Linux.  
  
One heads-up: the installers aren't signed yet, so your system will ask once the first time you open it. The website has the two-click fix.
